payload.headline: Amazon trades at the top of its value range while cash burn deepens

summary.thesis: Amazon is growing and its margins are widening, but it is burning cash and its price already sits at the top of its own historical value range, so there is little room for error.
summary.decision: Long-term: wait for a lower price. Swing: wait; there is no clean setup between support and resistance.
summary.act_at: Near 238.65 (mid value), or 251.93–257.04 support if the business improves

payload.happening: Amazon closed at 266.17, down 1.74% on the day. It was trading at 269.26 at 10:54 ET, which is not a close. The stock is in a downtrend but still sits above its 20-, 50- and 200-day averages (255.87, 254.41, 244.35), and all three averages are flat. The news is minor. Ring reportedly launched a home-security drone and a security robot for businesses, and a former AWS cloud executive was reported as the next infrastructure head at Meta. No earnings date is in the data.
payload.business: Several things are changing the business itself. Sales keep growing, with trailing 12-month revenue of 797.5B against 691.3B a year earlier. But growth is slowing: the latest quarter grew 12.09% from a year earlier, against 16.61% two quarters ago. Profitability is improving. Operating margin (profit from operations per dollar of sales) rose to 13.09% from 11.02%. Cash is the problem. Free cash flow (cash left after spending on operations and investment) was -46.9B over 12 months, against +10.6B a year earlier. That pushed Amazon to net debt of 66.7B (net cash of -66.7B). Heavy spending on data centers is the usual explanation for this kind of cash drain (general knowledge). The filings also flag unpaid customer bills up 61% while quarterly sales rose 12%. That can mean sales are being pulled forward or customers are paying more slowly. What is not at risk: liquidity (cash plus credit it can draw on) of 114.2B covers near-term needs, and share dilution is small at 0.77% a year. The Ring launches and the Meta hire change sentiment and headlines, not the numbers.

worth.text: There is no discounted-cash-flow value (a value built from projected future cash), because free cash flow is negative. The only method left compares price to sales against Amazon's own last 5 years. That gives 187.93 at the cheap end, 238.65 in the middle and 266.17 at the expensive end. Today's price equals the top of that range, and price-to-sales sits at the 80th percentile of its own 5-year history. Against earnings, the stock trades at 21.6 times trailing earnings and 20.8 times this year's estimate. It is 24.9 times next year's, because analysts expect next-year earnings per share of 10.67, below this year's 12.8. The filings note that the price needs about 34% a year growth, against 13% a year delivered over 3 years. The gap between the views comes down to the yardstick. Against its own history Amazon looks fully priced. Against peers it looks cheap, with price-to-sales of 3.6 against a peer median of 6.7 and a growth-adjusted ratio of 0.61 against peers.
worth.key_assumption: Amazon's price-to-sales stays within its own 5-year range rather than moving toward the higher peer median.

bull: Operating margin rose to 13.09% from 11.02%, so each dollar of sales now produces more operating profit.
Price-to-sales of 3.6 is well below the peer median of 6.7, and the growth-adjusted ratio of 0.61 against peers also points to cheap.
Next-year earnings estimates rose 1.4% over the last 30 days, and liquidity of 114.2B leaves room to keep investing.
bear: Free cash flow swung to -46.9B from +10.6B a year earlier, leaving net debt of 66.7B.
Quarterly revenue growth slowed to 12.09% from 16.61% two quarters ago, while the price needs about 34% a year growth.
Unpaid customer bills rose 61% while sales rose 12%, and next-quarter earnings estimates were cut 2.6% over 30 days.

levels.what: Today's close, equal to the top of the value range. Not a level to add at.
Bottom of the strongest support zone (251.93–257.04, 6 touches). A better entry if cash flow stabilises.
Midpoint of the own-history value range, where price and fair value meet.

longterm.why: The business is improving on margins but burning cash, and the price already reflects the top of its value range. The rule-based verdict is 'Too expensive', with a committee call of 'Avoid'.

swing.why: The trend is down and the price sits between support at 258.08–263.7 and resistance at 274.75–278.56, so a stop and a target give poor balance. Realized volatility (42.4) is above implied volatility (33.4), so recent swings have been larger than options are pricing.

decision.timing: No earnings date is in the data; options to 2026-11-20 price a move of about 4.3%, so a test of 258.08–263.7 support is the next point to reassess.

change_mind: Free cash flow over 12 months turning positive again (against -46.9B now), which would allow a cash-flow-based valuation.
A daily close below 251.93 would break the strongest support. A close above 278.56 would clear the first resistance and challenge the downtrend.
Quarterly revenue growth back to 16.61% or higher from 12.09%, alongside unpaid customer bills growing more slowly than the 61% now flagged.
